title: Vice-President addresses Valedictory Session of Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo 2026 in New Delhi
subtitle:
Environmental commitments are catalysts for India’s development, not hindrances to growth: Vice-President

India has answered global doubts by demonstrating that economic growth and reduced fossil fuel dependence can go hand in hand: Vice-President

India’s renewable energy transformation offers an inspiring model for the Global South: Vice-President

Clean energy transition must become a people’s movement, creating economic opportunities and household prosperity: Vice-President
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                05 NOV 2026 2:43PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today said that India’s remarkable progress in renewable energy demonstrates that environmental commitments are not a hindrance to economic growth but a catalyst for the country’s development journey.
Addressing the Valedictory Session of the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, the Vice-President highlighted India’s achievements in the renewable energy sector, its commitment to sustainable development and the transformative role of clean energy in empowering households, farmers and communities across the country.
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan addressed the Valedictory Session of the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, today.

He said that environmental commitments are catalysts for India’s development, not hindrances to growth, and highlighted how India has demonstrated that economic progress and reduced dependence on fossil fuels can go hand in hand.

Emphasising that the renewable energy transition must become a people’s movement, the Vice President highlighted India’s achievements in solar energy, the empowerment of households and farmers, and the importance of innovation and global cooperation.

He also observed that India’s renewable energy transformation offers an inspiring model for the Global South.

@mnreindia
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
November 5, 2026
Recalling the doubts about whether a developing country of India’s size could sustain rapid economic growth while reducing its dependence on fossil fuels, the Vice-President said that India had answered these doubts through its achievements.
He highlighted that India’s non-fossil fuel-based installed capacity has crossed 300 gigawatts and that the country achieved 50 per cent of its installed electricity capacity from non-fossil fuel sources in 2025, five years ahead of its commitment. Solar power capacity, he noted, has grown from less than 3 gigawatts to over 170 gigawatts over a decade.
Pointing out that solar power, which was once several times more expensive than coal-based electricity, is now among the cheapest sources of electricity in India, he said that this transformation reflects sound policies, private enterprise and the collective efforts of States and citizens.
The Vice-President observed that hydrogen energy is making encouraging progress in India and expressed confidence that advancements in science and technology would make hydrogen energy increasingly affordable in the years ahead. He said that India’s renewable energy transformation is not only an exemplary achievement for the country but also a model for the Global South.
The Vice-President said that the progress achieved over the last decade vindicates Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision that environmental commitments are catalysts for growth, delivering greater energy access, lower industrial costs, employment opportunities and reduced import dependence. Calling for stronger industry-academia collaboration, he said, “The technologies of 2040 will come from the laboratories and start-ups of today,” emphasising the importance of research, innovation and entrepreneurship.
The Vice-President said that over 65 lakh households have joined the solar movement under the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, gaining access to affordable clean energy. He further highlighted that nearly 30 lakh farmers have benefited under PM-KUSUM, observing that solar pumps help farmers save on diesel costs, earn additional income and become Urjadatas, givers of energy as well as food.
The Vice-President highlighted that initiatives under PM-JANMAN and the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan are extending electricity access to remote tribal areas where conventional grid connectivity may not be feasible. He observed that access to electricity transforms lives by expanding opportunities in education, healthcare, communication and livelihoods, emphasising that energy solutions must address the distinct needs of cities, villages and remote habitations.
Describing the renewable energy transition as a Jan Andolan, as envisioned by the Prime Minister, the Vice-President said that such a movement cannot be driven by the government alone.He urged the active participation of teachers, students, entrepreneurs and citizens.He noted that people’s participation in this movement would not only accelerate the adoption of renewable energy but also create new economic opportunities, generate livelihoods and promote household prosperity.
Invoking Mission LiFE, the Vice-President called for energy-efficient practices, mindful consumption and responsible disposal, observing that a billion small individual actions can contribute as significantly to sustainability as a new power plant.
The Vice-President said that the coming decade would be crucial for achieving global climate goals and reiterated India’s vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047 and net-zero emissions by 2070. He noted that India’s electricity demand could rise nearly seven-fold by 2070, emphasising the need to meet growing energy requirements through clean, reliable and affordable power while protecting the environment.
Urging participants to translate the Summit’s deliberations into action, the Vice-President said, “Turn discussions into projects, and projects into power.” He called for global cooperation, observing, “If the world is to be lit by the Sun, let it be lit by hands that work together.”
On the occasion, the Vice-President presented the Excellence in Renewable Energy Awards and PM Surya Ghar Awards to the best-performing States, government departments, vendors, brand owners and public sector banks.

The awards recognise outstanding contributions and achievements in advancing renewable energy adoption and strengthening India’s clean energy ecosystem.

title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi interacts with Indian Contingent that participated in Asian Para Games 2026
subtitle:
The phenomenal journey from 14 in 2010 to 114 medals is the ultimate testament to your relentless hard work and dedication: PM

Keeping the Olympics firmly in focus, from the ramparts of the Red Fort this time, I have urged our youth to step forward and participate in the talent hunt campaign: PM

The government has approved the Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing Scheme; It is now time for our sports goods manufacturing industry to achieve new milestones: PM

Whenever an Indian or foreign athlete steps onto the field, their sports gear, as well as their apparel and footwear, should be 'Made in India': PM

We want India to produce world-class players and also manufacture world-class sports equipment: PM
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                05 NOV 2026 7:52PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today interacted with the Indian contingent that participated in the Asian Para Games 2026 at Indira Gandhi Sports Complex in New Delhi. Speaking on the occasion, the Prime Minister stated that he had been eagerly waiting to meet the Para-Asian Games athletes after interacting with the Asian Games contingent a few weeks ago, and noted that their magnificent performance reflects India's rapid emergence as a major global sporting power. Congratulating the players on behalf of 140 crore citizens and felicitating their families, trainers, and coaches for their vital contributions, he stated that the athletes have won both medals on a grand stage and the hearts of millions across the nation.
Contrasting past eras when India's sporting participation was treated as a mere formality and the country lagged in para-sports with just one gold and 14 total medals at the 2010 Para Asian Games, the Prime Minister highlighted the contingent's historic leap to 114 medals comprising 30 gold, 35 silver, and 49 bronze alongside five world records and nine Asian records. Noting that 34 of the 56 female athletes won medals, Indian players swept all three podium spots in four events, and the contingent clinched nine gold medals on the final day alone, he praised their relentless drive to keep winning until the very end of the tournament. “This journey from 14 to 114 medals is the result of the pinnacle of your hard work,” observed PM Modi.
Spotlighting maiden gold medals won by Indian athletes in several events where the country had never succeeded before, the Prime Minister noted that Mona Agarwal set a world record in para shooting while Haney broke his own previous world record. “Through their performance, Himanshu, Ravi, and Jehan showed the world how physical challenges are to be defeated,” noted Shri Modi.
Observing that while the world witnesses the brilliance of individual or collective victory, the grand edifice of success rests on years of unseen toil, sweat, and unwavering penance, the Prime Minister recalled how athlete Rinku maintained his courage after losing his mother just two months before the Asian Para Games and honored her memory by lifting her photograph upon winning gold. “That moment made all of us emotional,” remarked PM Modi.
Describing the athletes' struggles and triumphs as deeply inspiring, the Prime Minister pointed out the close parallel between their personal journeys and the nation's own developmental trajectory. “Today your efforts and the country's efforts are coming together to become an unstoppable force,” affirmed Shri Modi.
the Prime Minister stated that just as the athletes refused to bow before adversity, the nation resolved to overhaul the system so youth talent would not go to waste, instilling confidence among young athletes that the country stands firmly behind them. Pointing to India's growing dominance in archery, athletics, shooting, swimming, table tennis, badminton, judo, and powerlifting, he noted that 36 of the 61 debutants at the Asian Para Games won medals while Sandeep set a world record on his debut. “This participation of the youth is both a picture of today's India and a proclamation of the India of the future,” asserted PM Modi.
Emphasizing that the government views sports not merely as national and international tournaments but as a vital medium for personality development and nation-building, the Prime Minister stated that athletics imparts essential life values to young citizens. “It is sports alone that teach the youth how to win after losing and explain the meaning of discipline and team spirit,” remarked Shri Modi.
Detailing efforts to build a modern sports ecosystem through school and grassroots campaigns, numerous Khelo India Centres, and Olympic-standard training under the TOPS scheme, the Prime Minister recalled his recent call from the Red Fort inviting youth to participate in a nationwide talent hunt campaign with an eye on the Olympics. “With this very vision, we are building a modern sports ecosystem for the country,” asserted PM Modi.
Highlighting that para-sports receive equal priority within these national initiatives to help athletes shine at major global events, the Prime Minister pointed to the tangible outcomes achieved at the recent tournament. “In this competition, players receiving assistance from TOPS won 41 medals, and Khelo India players won 19 medals, which shows that our efforts are moving forward in the right direction,” noted Shri Modi.
Observing that India's modern sports policies are generating wide-ranging youth opportunities beyond the playing field, the Prime Minister pointed to the rapid expansion of sports infrastructure construction, equipment manufacturing, and the broadcasting economy. “Today modern policies regarding sports in India are creating numerous new opportunities for the youth in the world of sports even outside the field,” observed PM Modi.
Noting the recent approval of the Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing Scheme worth over 1,800 crore rupees, the Prime Minister called upon the domestic sports manufacturing industry to ensure that athletes worldwide step onto the field wearing Made-in-India gear, apparel, and footwear, thereby strengthening MSMEs and creating jobs in small towns and rural areas. “We want India to produce world-class players and also manufacture world-class sports equipment,” asserted Shri Modi.
Urging the athletes during their upcoming visits to schools, colleges, and institutions to mentor youth on both on-field victory and off-field sports careers while highlighting government initiatives for Divyangjans, the Prime Minister noted the recent Cabinet decision increasing disability pensions, lowering the eligibility threshold from 80 percent to 40 percent, and extending pension coverage from birth rather than age 18, alongside creating a 10,000-word Indian Sign Language dictionary, providing sign-language schoolbooks, and making public spaces accessible under the Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan. “Our effort is that every Divyang brother and sister of the country gets respect, gets equal opportunities, and can move forward in life on the strength of their capability,” affirmed PM Modi.
Reminding the contingent that the Aichi-Nagoya podium is a launching pad rather than the final destination as India sets its sights on the Los Angeles 2028 Games, for which Avani and Manish have already secured quotas, the Prime Minister urged the athletes to celebrate their triumph and immediately begin preparations to ensure record participation and medal hauls in 2028 before concluding with his best wishes. “The country is with you, and the entire country is waiting for your next victory,” affirmed Shri Modi.

title: English rendering of PM's speech during interaction with India’s Asian Para Games Champions
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                05 NOV 2026 6:22PM by PIB Delhi
content:
My colleagues in the Cabinet, Shri Mansukh Mandaviya ji and Smt. Raksha Khadse ji, all representatives of the Paralympic Committee of India and the National Sports Federations, other distinguished guests, all medal-winning athletes, ladies and gentlemen.
I had been eagerly waiting to meet all of you. Just a few weeks ago, I met the athletes who participated in the Asian Games, and now I have got the opportunity to meet all of you energetic companions who participated in the Para Asian Games. Your outstanding performance shows that India is rapidly emerging as a major power in the world of sports. On such a large platform, you have not only won medals, but you have also won the hearts of crores of Indians. Once again, all of you para-athletes have demonstrated that the highest flights are achieved through determination and courage. On behalf of 140 crore countrymen, I congratulate all of you wholeheartedly.
Your families, trainers, and coaches have also played a crucial role in this achievement. I congratulate them as well. And as I have said before, the amount of effort a coach has to put in for an athlete is immense, but for a Paralympic athlete, many times more effort is required. Only then do such remarkable results emerge. Therefore, I extend special congratulations and appreciation to them.
Friends,
There was a time when India's participation in most sports was considered merely a formality. In para-sports too, the country was far behind. At the 2010 Asian Para Games, India won only one gold medal. Altogether, we managed to win just fourteen medals in that tournament. Fourteen. This time, however, our athletes have returned with one hundred and fourteen medals. Just think about this journey from fourteen to one hundred and fourteen. It is the result of the highest level of your hard work. It is the outcome of your dedication to sports and the ecosystem that has developed around it. This time, with thirty golds, thirty-five silvers, forty-nine bronzes, five new world records, and nine Asian records, you have filled the entire nation with pride. Out of fifty-six women athletes, thirty-four daughters became medal winners. And in four events, all three podium positions belonged to India. India won the gold, and in the same event, India also won the silver and the bronze. Even on the last day of the competition, you performed wonders by winning nine gold medals. It seemed as though you had decided that as long as the Games continued, the medal-winning streak would not stop.
Friends,
This time, our athletes won gold medals in disciplines where India had never achieved such success before. Mona Agarwal created a world record in para shooting. Honey broke his own previous world record. Himanshu, Ravi, and Jehan showed the world through their performances how physical challenges can be overcome.
Friends,
Whether it is the personal achievement of an athlete or the collective success of a nation, the world sees only the shine of victory. But the years of hard work behind that moment, the sweat shed day and night, and the unwavering dedication and perseverance required to reach that point are what form the foundation on which the towering structure of success stands. For example, Rinku ji lost her mother just two months before the Asian Para Games. Even amidst such great sorrow, she maintained her courage. And when she won the gold medal, she raised her mother's photograph and dedicated that medal to her. That moment touched the hearts of all Indians.
Friends,
Your struggles and achievements are an inspiration to every Indian. And in this journey, your path and the nation’s path have been very similar. That is why today, your efforts and the efforts of the nation are combining and creating an even greater force together.
Friends,
After 2014, when the country began its journey towards bigger goals, the situation was very different. Most parents were afraid to send their children into sports and the children themselves were often hesitant. There was disorder in the system, a lack of resources, a lack of support, and a lack of transparency. People used to say that nothing could change in such a system. They had accepted it as a reality. But just as you never accepted defeat before any challenge, the country too kept its eyes fixed only on its goals. We resolved that we would not allow the talent of our youth to go to waste. Therefore, we decided to change the very system that prevented young people like you from moving forward. As a result, a new approach towards sports emerged. Today, if a young athlete has faith in his or her talent, that athlete also believes that the country stands with them. Our para-sports ecosystem itself is one of the biggest examples of this. In sports where India’s representation was once extremely limited, our presence is now growing stronger. In archery, athletics, shooting, swimming, table tennis, badminton, judo, powerlifting, and many other sports, new young athletes are emerging. We are discovering new champions. This time, sixty-one of our athletes participated in the Asian Para Games for the first time. Sixty-one completely new athletes. And among those first-time participants, thirty-six returned home with medals. Sandeep even created a world record in his debut itself. This participation of young athletes reflects the India of today and announces the India of the future.
Friends,
We do not view sports merely as a collection of national and international events. For us, sports are also a powerful medium for character-building and nation-building. It is sports that teach young people how to win after losing. Sports teach discipline and the meaning of team spirit.
Friends,
With this vision, we are building a modern sports ecosystem for the country. Campaigns are being run at schools and at the grassroots level. A large number of Khelo India Centres have been established. We also launched the TOPS Scheme so that athletes could receive Olympic-level training. Keeping the Olympics in mind, I called upon young people from the Red Fort this time to come forward through the Talent Hunt campaign.
Friends,
Para-sports are being given equal importance in all these efforts. As a result, athletes like you are emerging with excellence and bringing glory to the nation at major events. We saw this once again in the recently concluded Para Games. In this competition, athletes receiving support under TOPS won forty-one medals, while Khelo India athletes won nineteen medals. This shows that our efforts are moving in the right direction.
Friends,
Today, modern sports policies in India are creating many new opportunities for young people, even beyond the playing field. Sports infrastructure development, sports equipment production, and the sports broadcasting economy are all expanding rapidly.
Friends,
Just a few days ago, the government approved the Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing Scheme worth more than ₹1,800 crore. Now it is time for our sports goods manufacturing industry to achieve new milestones. When an Indian or foreign athlete steps onto a field anywhere in the world, their sports gear should also be Made in India. Their clothing and footwear should also be Made in India. We want India to produce not only world-class athletes but also world-class sports equipment. We want Indian sports products to reach markets across the world. This will strengthen India’s MSME sector and create new opportunities in small towns and rural areas.
Friends,
After today’s event, all of you will also be invited to schools, colleges, and various institutions, where young people will want to listen to you and learn from you. When you speak with them, teach them the secrets of winning on the field, but also tell them about the opportunities connected with sports beyond the field. And you should also explain to them the extensive efforts being made by the country to make life easier for our differently-abled brothers and sisters. Just a few days ago, the Cabinet took an important decision regarding pensions for persons with disabilities. We increased the pension amount. The disability benchmark that was previously 80 percent has been reduced to 40 percent. Earlier, a person had to be eighteen years old to become eligible for a pension. Now, the path for pensions has been opened even for eligible children with disabilities from birth. Similarly, significant efforts have been made to promote Indian Sign Language. A sign language dictionary containing more than ten thousand words has been developed. School textbooks are also being made available in sign language. Through the Accessible India Campaign, public places are being made more accessible for persons with disabilities. Our effort is to ensure that every differently-abled person in the country receives both dignity and equal opportunities, and is able to move forward in life on the strength of their own abilities.
Friends,
The podium at Aichi-Nagoya is not the final destination of your journey. Keep that in mind. You should use this success as a launching pad for even bigger goals. The next target for India, and for most of you athletes, is L.A. 2028. Avani and Manish have already secured their quota places for Los Angeles. Our goal should be to ensure that as many Indian athletes as possible participate in L.A. 2028 and bring home as many medals as possible. Therefore, celebrate this moment wholeheartedly, but also begin preparing for the next challenge right away. The country stands with you, and so do I. The entire nation is waiting for your next victory. Once again, many congratulations and best wishes to all of you.
The grand festival of Diwali has already begun. This time, celebrate Diwali with great pride, enthusiasm, and splendour. But along with celebrating Diwali, also set your next goal in your mind and move forward with a new resolve. My very best wishes to all of you.
Thank you very much.

India is emerging among the early global pioneers in Space debris removal, with an Indian Startup advancing technologies to make outer space safer and more sustainable, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh said today.
Announcing a vision of achieving debris-free Space by 2030, the Minister said India's emerging capabilities in active space debris removal reflect the country's growing global leadership in space technology and its commitment to ensuring a safe space environment for the entire humanity.
Dr. Jitendra Singh was speaking virtually from Kartavya Bhawan, New Delhi, at the inauguration of Cosmoserve Space's Base 1 facility in Hyderabad.
The inauguration ceremony at VSD Tech Park, Gachibowli, Hyderabad, was attended by Shri D. Sridhar Babu, Minister for IT and Industries, Government of Telangana, as Guest of Honour, and Dr Chiranjeevi Phanindra, Founder and CEO, Cosmoserve Space. Dr. Jitendra Singh joined the programme virtually as Chief Guest.
Congratulating Cosmoserve Space on the inauguration, Dr. Jitendra Singh said Base 1 is a comprehensive, state-of-the-art facility spread across approximately 14,800 square feet, where space robots are designed, built, tested under space conditions and operated through mission control. The facility houses specialised capabilities including orbital rendezvous and capture labs, space robotics innovation labs, microgravity simulation platforms and satellite integration clean rooms, marking a significant advancement in India's private space capabilities.
The Minister congratulated Dr. Chiranjeevi Phanindra and his team for pioneering work in active debris removal (ADR) and in-orbit servicing. Mission EMBRACE, which conducted an in-space test of soft robotic petals in July 2026 within a year of the company's formation, reflects the rapid progress and growing technological maturity of India's private space startups. He appreciated the team's experience in ISRO and the Gaganyaan programme being translated into a collaborative model in the private sector.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said Cosmoserve Space's partnerships with Pixel for satellite systems, Dhruv Aerospace Netherlands for propulsion systems and Skyroot Aerospace for launch services demonstrate an emerging culture of end-to-end collaboration in space technology. The initiative showcases how Indian startups are combining indigenous payloads, battery technologies, satellite systems and private launch capabilities to build integrated space missions and establish global benchmarks.
Crediting Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's transformative space reforms for unlocking India's immense potential, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the journey initiated around five to six years ago, followed by the establishment of NewSpace India Limited and IN-SPACe, has fundamentally reshaped the country's space ecosystem. India's space economy has grown to nearly USD 9 billion and is projected to reach USD 40–45 billion in the coming decade, while its space startup ecosystem has expanded from a single-digit number to nearly 450 enterprises.
The Minister said India never lacked scientific talent or technological capabilities; what was needed was an enabling ecosystem to unlock the immense potential of its youth. He called upon domestic and international investors to participate more actively in the space sector and urged greater philanthropy in science and research to accelerate innovation, strengthen collaborations and support emerging technologies.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said India's ultimate objective remains technological self-reliance and sovereign capabilities, alongside international partnerships. India's achievements in Chandrayaan and the Gaganyaan programme demonstrate its ability to undertake sophisticated missions at significantly lower costs. He also emphasised that India's space capabilities are transforming life on Earth through applications in Gati Shakti, smart cities, disaster preparedness and several other areas directly benefiting citizens.
The Minister said Cosmoserve Space's initiative embodies the spirit of Vishwa bandhu Bharat, extending India's commitment to space sustainability beyond national boundaries to the benefit of humanity. He congratulated the team for contributing to a cleaner and safer space environment and said such initiatives would strengthen India's global leadership in space technology and enhance its geopolitical stature.
Dr. Jitendra Singh expressed his eagerness to visit the facility in person at the earliest opportunity and interact with the Cosmoserve Space team.

title: Union Minister Shri G. Kishan Reddy Calls for Accelerated Coal Sector Reforms, Coal Gasification and Technology-Driven Mining to Strengthen India's Energy Security
subtitle: At the 4th Conference of Mining Ministers, Minister Highlights Coal Gasification, Critical Minerals, AI-driven Technologies and Stronger Centre-State Collaboration
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                05 NOV 2026 6:44PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Minister of Coal and Mines, Shri G. Kishan Reddy, addressing the 4th Conference of Mining Ministers on Reforms in the Mines and Coal Sector in Goa, highlighted the transformative journey of India's coal and mining sectors under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. He emphasised that sustained reforms have enhanced transparency, efficiency and professionalism, strengthening the sectors' contribution to national economic growth and energy security.
Focusing on the priorities of the coal sector, Shri G. Kishan Reddy underscored the need to accelerate Coal Gasification for the optimum utilisation of India's abundant coal resources. He highlighted its potential to unlock the economic value of domestic coal, promote industrial diversification, generate employment and strengthen the country's long-term energy security.
Highlighting the strategic importance of Critical Minerals in the evolving global geopolitical landscape, the Minister stressed the need to strengthen domestic exploration, mining, processing, refining and recycling capabilities. He emphasised that developing a self-reliant mineral ecosystem is essential to reducing import dependence and strengthening India's strategic and economic resilience.
Emphasising the transformative role of technology, Shri Reddy called upon State Governments to harness Artificial Intelligence (AI), digitalisation and advanced technological solutions across exploration, mine operations and mineral recovery. He highlighted that technology-driven practices would improve productivity, operational efficiency and sustainability in the mining and coal sectors.
The Minister urged States to expedite the operationalization of auctioned mines, accelerate the auction of new blocks, expand exploration activities and adopt technology-driven practices to unlock the full potential of their mineral resources. He also highlighted how mining sector reforms have strengthened State economies, attracted investments, generated employment opportunities and enhanced revenue generation, while promoting development in mining-affected regions.
Reaffirming the spirit of Cooperative Federalism, Shri G. Kishan Reddy called for stronger coordination between the Centre and States to unlock India's mineral and coal potential, strengthen the mining ecosystem and ensure sustainable and inclusive growth. He expressed confidence that collective efforts and a shared roadmap would take India's mining and coal sectors to new heights, contributing significantly to the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.
Addressing the conference, Union Minister of State for Coal and Mines, Shri Satish Chandra Dubey, stated that the mining sector is a key pillar of the country's economic progress, industrial development and energy security. He highlighted the wide-ranging reforms being undertaken by the Central Government, including transparent auction processes, promotion of investment, creation of new employment opportunities and efforts to accelerate mining activities.
He emphasized the importance of prioritizing sustainable and responsible mining, environmental protection, mine rehabilitation and the welfare of communities residing in mining-affected areas. He stated that plans for post-mining rehabilitation and the creation of alternative livelihood opportunities for local communities should be incorporated from the very beginning of mining operations to ensure that environmental and social interests are protected alongside development.
He also stressed the need to increase coal production while promoting safe and modern mining technologies, coal gasification, innovations in coal utilisation and initiatives such as First Mile Connectivity. Furthermore, he called upon States to share their experiences and best practices and work towards addressing challenges in the mining sector.
Addressing the conference, Secretary, Ministry of Coal, Shri Vikram Dev Dutt, highlighted the significant progress made by India's coal sector and its vital role in strengthening the country's energy security and driving economic growth.
He noted that domestic coal production had surpassed one billion tonnes for the second consecutive year, marking a significant achievement in India's journey towards energy self-reliance and reducing dependence on imported coal.
Shri Vikram Dev Dutt emphasised the importance of continued structural reforms to make the coal sector more competitive, transparent, efficient and investment-friendly. Highlighting key initiatives such as Commercial Coal Mining, the revised SHAKTI framework and Coal SETU, he underlined the need to promote greater private sector participation, simplify processes and accelerate the operationalisation of coal mines.
He highlighted Coal Gasification as a major opportunity for value addition, industrial diversification and employment generation. He urged coal-bearing States to actively facilitate investments, support infrastructure development and accelerate project implementation to realise the sector's immense potential.
Stressing the importance of technology, digitalisation, sustainable mining practices and efficient logistics, the Secretary called for stronger Centre-State collaboration to unlock the full potential of India's coal and mineral resources.
He reiterated that the next phase of growth in the coal sector must move beyond extraction towards value creation, positioning the sector as a catalyst for industrial development, stronger State revenues, employment generation and the vision of Viksit Bharat.
At the conference, Ms. Rupinder Brar, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Coal, delivered a detailed and comprehensive presentation highlighting the recent reforms undertaken in the coal sector, their role in enhancing Ease of Doing Business, and the key challenges and expectations from States. The presentation outlined how these reforms are simplifying procedures, improving transparency, facilitating investments and creating a more business-friendly environment for stakeholders. It also emphasised the importance of stronger Centre-State collaboration in addressing emerging challenges and accelerating the pace of reforms. These initiatives are paving the way for a more efficient, competitive and sustainable coal sector, thereby contributing to India's energy security and economic growth.
The Ministry of Mines, Government of India, organised the 4th Conference of Mining Ministers on 5–6 November 2026 in Goa, bringing together Mining Ministers from various States and senior officials from the Central and State Governments. The conference provided an important platform for interaction and exchange of views on various aspects of the mining sector. Discussions focused on the progress, opportunities and challenges in the sector, while encouraging States to share their experiences, initiatives and best practices.
The deliberations at the 4th Conference of Mining Ministers reaffirmed the importance of continued reforms and coordinated efforts between the Central and State Governments in strengthening India's coal sector.
With a focus on accelerating coal gasification, promoting commercial coal mining, leveraging advanced technologies, facilitating investments and ensuring sustainable mining practices, the Ministry of Coal remains committed to unlocking the full potential of India's domestic coal resources. The emphasis on value addition, operational efficiency, private sector participation and cooperative federalism will play a crucial role in positioning India's coal sector as a key driver of industrial growth, energy security, employment generation and economic development.

title: India Advances Global Diamond Industry Agenda Ahead of Kimberley Process Plenary
subtitle: India’s Observer Status in ADPA Strengthens Engagement with Diamond-Producing Countries
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                05 NOV 2026 6:32PM by PIB Delhi
content:
India, as Chair of the Kimberley Process (KP) for 2026, convened a stakeholder consultation in Luanda, Angola, on 3 November 2026, bringing together the Chairs and Vice-Chairs of KP Working Groups and Committees (KP Working Bodies), the KP Vice-Chair, Republic of Ghana, and the former KP Chair, United Arab Emirates. The consultation, led by KP Chair and Additional Secretary, Department of Commerce, Shri Yashvir Singh, focused on key priorities concerning the global diamond industry, including responsible rough diamond sourcing, institutional governance, compliance and consumer confidence. Representatives of Observers and partner organisations, including the World Diamond Council, KP Civil Society Coalition, Diamond Development Initiative (DDI) at RESOLVE and the African Diamond Producers’ Association (ADPA), also participated. The engagement formed part of India's outreach ahead of the KP Plenary to be held in New Delhi from 30 November to 4 December 2026. The consultation was held on the sidelines of the 20th anniversary celebrations of ADPA (ADPA@20), held in Luanda on 3–4 November 2026.
India has Observer status in ADPA, providing an institutional platform for engagement with African diamond-producing countries. This offers opportunities for cooperation in securing rough diamond supply chains, technical knowledge exchange, value addition, market access and the promotion of ethical and sustainable practices.
The Chairs and Vice-Chairs of the KP Working Bodies shared updates on progress against their respective work plans and outlined matters proposed for consideration at the Plenary. These included draft Administrative Decisions, initiatives relating to responsible rough diamond sourcing, improvements to the statistical reporting platform, and measures to strengthen institutional governance and participant compliance. The consultation also provided an opportunity to identify matters requiring further coordination and areas where early convergence could support the work of the Plenary.
Reaffirming India's KP Chairship theme of Confidence, Compliance and Credibility, the consultation provided an opportunity for an open exchange on the status and evolving priorities of the global diamond industry. Discussions covered the sustainability of diamond-producing countries and communities, sustainable funding and continuity of the KP Secretariat, digitalisation of certification and statistical processes, and strengthening compliance with the Kimberley Process Certification Scheme. Participants also exchanged views on the reform of the conflict diamond definition, responsible sourcing, artisanal and alluvial diamond production, consumer confidence and the importance of effective reporting and peer-review mechanisms.
Additional Secretary, Department of Commerce, and KP Chair, Shri Yashvir Singh, said, “India’s Chairship places emphasis on Confidence, Compliance and Credibility. The consultation in Luanda provided an opportunity to engage directly with the leadership of the KP Working Bodies, the KP Vice-Chair and Observers on issues that are important to the future of the Process and the diamond industry. Our endeavour is to build a shared understanding of the issues before the New Delhi Plenary and to advance practical outcomes through constructive dialogue and consensus-based decision-making.”
The African Diamond Producers’ Association (ADPA), established on 4 November 2006 in Luanda, Angola, seeks to enhance cooperation among African diamond-producing nations. ADPA comprises 15 effective member countries and 8 Observers, including two non-African Observers, namely the Russian Federation and India. Its member countries collectively account for over 60 per cent of global diamond production. ADPA is currently chaired by the Republic of Sierra Leone, represented by Minister of Mines and Mineral Resources, Hon. Julius Daniel Mattai. On 4 November 2026, Botswana was admitted as an Observer Member of ADPA during the 13th Extraordinary Meeting of the ADPA Council of Ministers held in Luanda.
On 4 November 2026,  Shri Yashvir Singh, participated in the Council of Ministers and main commemoration programme of ADPA@20 and delivered a presentation titled “Partnering for the Future: A Global Industry Perspective on Africa’s Diamond Future”. Speaking as KP Chair (India) 2026, he underlined the central place of African producing countries in the global diamond value chain and outlined how partnership between producers, manufacturing centres and consumer markets can support the long-term sustainability of the natural diamond sector. Drawing on India’s vision of the 3Cs – Confidence, Compliance and Credibility – he highlighted that consumer confidence in natural diamonds, robust compliance with KP minimum requirements and a credible, inclusive Kimberley Process are essential to ensuring that diamond resources continue to contribute to development in producing countries.
The programme brought together representatives of African diamond-producing countries, industry and other stakeholders to mark ADPA’s two decades of engagement. Sessions included discussions on the ADPA Sustainable Diamond Standard and the ADPA Business Council, perspectives on sustainability and audit practices, and deliberations on protecting the integrity of natural diamonds, industry advocacy, market differentiation and consumer confidence.
The 13th Extraordinary Meeting of the ADPA Council of Ministers, held alongside the 20th anniversary celebrations, approved a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Gem & Jewellery Export Promotion Council (GJEPC), India, and ADPA. The MoU seeks to strengthen cooperation between the Indian gem and jewellery industry and African diamond-producing countries, including through capacity building and skills development in diamond sorting, valuation and manufacturing, exchange of technical expertise, and the promotion of trade and investment linkages across the diamond value chain.
The discussions in Luanda will advance preparations for the KP Plenary in New Delhi, scheduled from 30 November to 4 December 2026 at Bharat Mandapam. The KP Plenary will be preceded by the New Delhi Diamond Dialogue (KP Forum) on 29 November 2026, with associated programme engagements extending through 5 December 2026. India will host the KP Plenary for the third time, following its previous Chairships in 2008 and 2019.
The Kimberley Process Certification Scheme (KPCS), established pursuant to United Nations General Assembly Resolution 55/56 (2000), is an international initiative aimed at preventing conflict diamonds from entering the legitimate rough diamond trade. The KP operates through a tripartite framework comprising Governments, the diamond industry and civil society. It currently has 60 Participants representing 86 countries, with the European Union and its Member States participating as a single entity. The Chairship of the Kimberley Process rotates annually among its participating countries, and India assumed the Chairship on 1 January 2026.

title: Department of Posts Takes Special Campaign 6 to the Last Mile-  Exceeds Targets
subtitle:
Cleaned 1,50,000 Sites

Resolved 1,50,000 Public Grievances and Disposed off 1,500 Appeals

Disposed over 8 lakh kg of scrap and 58,514 kg of e-waste worth ₹3.01 crore
date:

                05 NOV 2026 7:49PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Posts, Ministry of Communications, successfully conducted
Special Campaign 6
from 2nd to 31st October 2026, across its extensive nationwide network, reaffirming its commitment to institutionalising Swachhata, improving administrative efficiency, promoting environmental sustainability and strengthening citizen-centric service delivery.
The campaign witnessed significant achievements across its key focus areas. The Department resolved 1,50,000 public grievances and disposed of 1,500 appeals during the campaign. Against the target of cleanliness activities at 1.35 lakh sites, the Department covered 1,50,000 sites across the country. The campaign also resulted in freeing up 2,03,570 sq. ft. of office space for productive utilisation.
Swachhata: Taking the Last-Mile Approach
The Department adopted a comprehensive approach to Swachhata, covering cleanliness, efficient record management, disposal of redundant material, scientific waste management, optimum space utilisation and process simplification. Cleanliness drives were conducted across Post Offices, including Branch Post Offices, mail offices and administrative establishments, with a focus on public-facing and common areas.
The campaign also promoted Waste to Wealth through reuse of discarded materials, plantation and beautification initiatives. Notably, Mail Motor Services, Kolkata, renovated an office chamber using recycled wooden scrap, showcasing innovative resource utilisation.
Scientific Waste Management and Environmental Sustainability
A major thrust of Special Campaign 6 was the scientific management of scrap and e-waste. The disposal of over 8.03 lakh kg of scrap and 58,514 kg of e-waste generated revenue of approximately ₹3.01 crore during the campaign, while also contributing to better space utilisation and environmentally responsible disposal practices.
Postal Circles undertook several innovative initiatives to promote environmental sustainability. Assam Circle introduced Vertical Green Walls at its N-Gen Post Offices by converting discarded plastic waste and containers into planters, with participation from students. Mail Motor Services, Naraina, New Delhi, inducted 16 electric vehicles into its fleet on 29th October 2026, reinforcing the Department's commitment to greener transportation.
Other initiatives included plantation drives, awareness programmes on waste segregation and composting, and community participation in supporting clean surroundings.

Jan Sampark – Dak Chaupal: Bringing Government Services to Citizens
Under Special Campaign 6, the Department organised Dak Chaupals to strengthen citizen engagement and bring Government services closer to the people. The initiative focused on digital interface and financial inclusion with particular emphasis on last-mile delivery. Citizens were sensitised about Postal Life Insurance (PLI), Rural Postal Life Insurance (RPLI), India Post Payments Bank, Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), e-commerce, export services, and various Government welfare schemes.
These interactions offered an opportunity to address public grievances, obtain citizen feedback, and improve awareness about the range of services offered by India Post.

Dedicated One-Day Nationwide Activities under Special Campaign 6
In response to the initiative of the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG), the Department of Posts organised a dedicated one-day nationwide programme on 23rd October 2026. A total of 1,861 Dak Chaupals were organised across the country in which 76,343 citizens including 31,728 women took part and cleanliness activities were undertaken at approximately 55,952 sites. The programme also saw the resolution of 9,007 public grievances.
Special Campaign 6 also featured innovative community engagement activities. At Nehru Place Post Office a calligraphy activity on Swachhata and environmental awareness was organised for school children while, at Vasant Kunj Post Office, children took part in clay pot painting and plantation activities. These events were aimed at inculcating the concept of Swachhata and environmental responsibility among young minds.

The initiative leverages the extensive reach of India Post to facilitate the delivery of digitally generated citizen services through its physical postal network.
The Department also encouraged the adoption of technology-driven initiatives to strengthen transparency and improve service delivery. Odisha Circle and Jammu & Kashmir Postal Circles introduced a QR code-based customer feedback mechanisms, enabling customers to submit feedback in multiple languages, upload photographs and highlight service-related issues.

title: TRAI releases Recommendations on ‘The Framework for Satellite Communication Network Provider Authorisation, and Assignment of Spectrum to Satellite Communication Network Providers'
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                05 NOV 2026 5:00PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has today released its recommendations on
‘the Framework for Satellite Communication Network Provider Authorisation, and Assignment of Spectrum to Satellite Communication Network Providers’
.
Earlier, DoT conveyed to TRAI on 03.07.2025 that
"the Government proposes the introduction of a Satellite Communication Network (SCN) Authorisation under Section 3(1)(b) of the Telecommunications Act 2023”
and requested TRAI to
"provide terms and conditions for Satellite Communication Network (SCN) authorisation including provision of assignment of spectrum for both feeder link as well as user link under such authorisation”
.
In this regard, TRAI issued a consultation paper on ‘the Framework for Satellite Communication Network Authorisation, and Assignment of Spectrum to Satellite Communication Network Providers' on 08.04.2026. In response, comments from 31 stakeholders and counter-comments from 12 stakeholders were received and uploaded on the TRAI website.  An Open House Discussion (OHD) on the consultation paper was held on 02.07.2026 through virtual mode.
After considering the comments and counter-comments received from stakeholders in the consultation process, and further analysis, TRAI has finalized its recommendations on ‘the Framework for Satellite Communication Network Provider Authorisation, and Assignment of Spectrum to Satellite Communication Network Providers’.
Key highlights of the TRAI's recommendations:
Satellite Communication Network Provider Authorisation
A new authorisation - namely “Satellite Communication Network Provider Authorisation” - should be introduced under Section 3(1)(b) of the Telecommunications Act, 2023.
The Satellite Communication Network (SCN) provider authorised entities may provide Satellite Communication Network as a Service (SCNaaS) to eligible service providers.
The Satellite Communication Network (SCN) provider authorised entities may not provide telecommunication services directly to users.
The SCN provider authorisation should be for the national area, with a maximum duration of 20 years and provision for renewal for up to 20 years.
Fixed Satellite Service (FSS), Mobile Satellite Service (MSS), Direct-to-Device (D2D) services via satellite using MSS, and D2D services via satellite using IMT spectrum should be permitted through the satellite communication networks of SCN provider authorised entities.
The SCN provider authorised entities may seek appropriate satellite spectrum (FSS and MSS) from the Central Government and/ or utilize the spectrum assigned to partnering service providers - for providing satellite communication network as a service (SCNaaS) to eligible service providers.
Any licensee or authorised entity that is permitted to provide satellite-based communication services or provide telecommunication services through satellite network should be eligible to seek SCNaaS from SCN provider authorised entity.
Apart from SCN provider authorised entities, any entity holding any of the following licenses/ authorisations should also be permitted to provide SCNaaS to any authorised entity or licensee that is permitted to provide satellite-based communication services or provide telecommunication services through satellite network:
(a)    Unified service authorisation, access service authorisation, internet service authorisation and long distance service authorisation under the Telecommunications (Authorisation for Principal Telecom Services) Rules, 2026;
(b)   Access Service authorization, Internet Service authorization, NLD Service authorization, Commercial VSAT CUG Service authorization and GMPCS Service authorization under Unified License; and
(c)    License for Provision and Operation of Satellite Based Services Using Gateway Installed in India Under ‘
Sui-Generis
’ Category:
Provided that such entity fulfils the eligibility criteria for obtaining SCN provider authorisation and undertakes to abide by the technical and operating conditions, roll out obligations, and security conditions applicable to SCN provider authorisation.
Assignment of spectrum to SCN provider authorised entities
SCN provider authorised entities should be permitted to seek the assignment of - (a) FSS spectrum for feeder link, and (b) FSS spectrum and/or MSS spectrum for user links - from the Government.
The SCN provider authorised entity should be assigned FSS spectrum for deploying in the feeder link on an administrative basis. For seeking administrative assignment of FSS/ MSS spectrum for deploying in user links, SCN provider authorised entity should demonstrate that the intended service to be provided by its partnering service provider(s) by using the spectrum falls in the First Schedule of the Telecommunications Act, 2023.
Subject to alignment with the allocations in National Frequency Allocation Plan (NFAP) 2025, spectrum should be assigned to SCN provider authorised entities in the following frequency bands:

FSS spectrum and MSS spectrum should be assigned to SCN provider authorised entities for a period of up to five years. However, considering the market conditions, the Government may extend it for a further period of up to two years.
Terms and conditions, including pricing, for assignment of FSS spectrum and MSS spectrum to SCN provider authorised entities, should remain valid for a period of five years from the date of notification of the policy regime by the Central Government, further extendable by a period of upto two years.
Any revision in the terms and conditions, including pricing, for assignment of FSS spectrum and MSS spectrum to SCN provider authorised entities, notified by the Central Government after a period of five years from the date of notification of the policy regime, should become applicable to all SCN provider authorised entities including the existing SCN provider authorised entities.
The SCN provider authorised entity should be permitted to enter into an agreement with any eligible service authorised entity ("partnering entity”) to utilise –
the FSS spectrum held by the partnering entity for using the spectrum in feeder links; and
the FSS/ MSS spectrum held by its partnering entity for using the spectrum in user links -
for the limited purpose of providing satellite communication network as a service (SCNaaS) to the partnering entity, while the right to use of spectrum should remain with the partnering entity.
MSS-based D2D Service
MSS-based D2D services [i.e. direct-to-device (D2D) services via satellite by using the spectrum in L-band and S-band allocated for mobile satellite service (MSS)] should be permitted in India.
The entities authorised to provide access service should be permitted to seek SCNaaS from SCN provider authorised entities for providing MSS-based D2D services.
After acceptance of these recommendations, the Central Government should encourage smartphone handset manufacturers to include the necessary modules for supporting the applicable MSS bands in future smartphone handsets sold in India.
IMT-based D2D Service
IMT-based D2D service [i.e. direct-to-device (D2D) services via satellite by using IMT spectrum should be permitted in the country on non-interference, non-protection basis under the provisions of Article 4.4 of ITU Radio Regulations - without waiting for the outcome of WRC-27.
The decision taken by the Government of India, if any, on the matter of IMT-based D2D service after the conclusion of WRC-2027 should be made applicable to IMT-based D2D service at that stage.
Any entity authorised to provide access service and holding IMT spectrum, should be permitted to provide the IMT-based D2D service by availing SCNaaS from any SCN provider authorised entity. Conversely, any SCN provider authorised entity should be permitted to provide SCNaaS to any entity, which is authorised to provide access service and holds IMT spectrum:
Provided
that the provision of IMT-based D2D service is permitted only if one or more entities authorised to provide access service – together holding the assignment of the relevant IMT frequency channel across all 22 licensed service areas of the country – agree to allow the usage of their IMT frequency channel by the SCN provider authorised entity for the purpose of providing SCNaaS to only such entity (ies).
The IMT frequency bands under frequency division duplexing (FDD) arrangement viz. 600 MHz, 700 MHz, 800 MHz, 900 MHz, 1800 MHz, and 2100 MHz band should be permitted to be used for providing the IMT-based D2D service.
The frequency allocation table of the National Frequency Allocation Plan (NFAP) should be amended to include Mobile Satellite Service (MSS) as a secondary service in the frequency bands identified for the IMT-based D2D service. An India-specific footnote should be introduced to clarify that the secondary MSS operations in such frequency bands will be limited to the IMT-based D2D service, which will operate on a non-interference and non-protection basis to both domestic and cross-border operations.
For protecting the incumbent services operating in the country from any harmful interference arising from the IMT-based D2D service, limits on electric field strength of aggregate signal from all beams should be specified.
Financial Conditions
In determining the applicable rate of Authorisation Fee, Spectrum Charges and financial conditions for SCN Provider Authorised Entities, including definition of GR/ ApGR/ AGR and other financial conditions, TRAI has followed the principle of maintaining regulatory parity between vertically integrated service model and an unbundled shared network model of providing satellite-based services.
Definition of GR/ ApGR/ AGR & treatment of SCNaaS charges:
Gross Revenue (GR) shall include all revenues accruing to the SCN Provider Authorised Entity for provision of Satellite Communications Network-as-a-Service (SCNaaS) to eligible Service Authorised Entities for the provision of satellite based services to end users, and any other revenue from network-related activities, without any set-off for related items of expenditure.
The SCNaaS Charges paid by eligible Service Authorised entity (including eligible VNOs) to an SCN provider authorised entity, under a commercial service agreement for provisioning of SCNaaS, which are reported as revenue by the SCN Provider Authorised entity, should be permitted as deduction from the ApGR of the Service Authorised entity, subject to proper documentation and verification.
For determination of Applicable Gross Revenue (ApGR), non-telecom revenue should be excluded from Gross Revenue, in line with provisions under Telecommunications (Authorisation for Provision of Principal Telecommunication Services) Rules, 2026
For determination of AGR, charges paid to another SCN Provider Authorised entity for utilization of satellite earth station gateway(s) should be allowed as deductions, along with GST paid to government (if applicable)
Authorisation Fee:
Authorisation Fee for SCN Provider Authorised entities should be 8% of the Adjusted Gross Revenue. There should be no Minimum Authorisation Fee for the same.
Spectrum Charges:
Spectrum Charges for an SCN provider authorised entity should be based on AGR, with a differential between urban and rural areas for NGSO based FSS (which can be a per subscriber additional charge for urban area) and should have the same charging rate and framework as that applicable for satellite based commercial communication services, as decided by DoT on basis of Recommendations dated 09.05.2025.
Spectrum assigned to an SCN Provider Authorised entity should attract an annual Minimum Spectrum Charge of Rs. 3,500 per MHz, in case FSS/ MSS spectrum is assigned to such entity by the Central Government.
In case MSS spectrum (L/S band) is used for providing D2D service, the spectrum charging framework should be the same as when used for providing conventional MSS on specialized devices.
In case IMT Spectrum assigned to Service authorized entity is used for providing D2D service, no additional spectrum charges should be levied on the partnering Access Service provider for utilisation of their assigned IMT spectrum in user link for providing satellite-based D2D services. The existing spectrum charging framework applicable for the assigned IMT spectrum should continue to apply.
Spectrum charges for providing satellite-based services by Service providers under existing Unified License or new Telecommunications (Authorisation for Provision of Principal Telecommunication Services) Rules 2026, should be levied only on that portion of their AGR as derived from FSS & MSS (including MSS to normal & specialized phones).
Spectrum charges for SCNaaS provided by eligible service providers should be levied only on that portion of their AGR as derived from provisioning of SCNaaS.

These recommendations of TRAI envision the development of a robust and competitive satellite communication ecosystem in India. The recommended framework for SCN provider authorisation would enable efficient utilisation of satellite network infrastructure and spectrum through SCNaaS and facilitate innovative satellite-based services, including D2D connectivity using MSS as well as IMT spectrum. This would provide greater flexibility to service providers in accessing satellite network resources and support the expansion of satellite-based connectivity across the country.

title: MINISTRY OF CULTURE SIGNS MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING WITH GOOGLE ARTS & CULTURE TO DIGITISE AND SHARE INDIA’S CULTURAL HERITAGE
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                05 NOV 2026 7:33PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Culture, Government of India, today signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Google Arts & Culture to bring India’s cultural heritage to the public through cutting-edge digital tools. The MoU was signed at a virtual ceremony in the presence of Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture, and Mr Amit Sood, Vice President and Founder, Google Arts & Culture.
The partnership will reflect the civilisational breadth of India: the monuments and archaeological sites protected by the Archaeological Survey of India and the collections they hold, the holdings of the national museums, the manuscript heritage being documented under Gyan Bharatam, and the crafts, performing arts and living traditions sustained by the Ministry’s institutions across the country.
At its centre is the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum, taking shape in the North and South Blocks of New Delhi as a museum of India’s history across the ages. Its digitisation will create a lasting record of the buildings and the wealth of artefacts they will house, and offer the public an early window onto one of the most significant cultural undertakings of our time.
The MoU is part of the Ministry’s wider effort to strengthen accessibility and expand its digital initiatives, so that India’s heritage can be explored in Indian languages and on any device. It reflects a whole-of-Ministry approach in which preservation, public access and the growth of India’s creative economy advance together, drawing on institutions of every scale and partners from across sectors.
Commenting on the partnership, Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture, said: “India’s cultural heritage is a living inheritance. It belongs to every citizen and speaks to the whole world. Our partnership with Google Arts & Culture brings technology to bear on documenting, preserving and sharing that inheritance, from our ancient manuscripts and monuments to the collections of our national museums and the upcoming Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum. By making these treasures available in Indian languages and to audiences across the globe, we hope to bring more people closer to the story of Indian civilisation, and to safeguard it for generations to come.”
Google Arts & Culture has had a long association with the Ministry’s institutions, including the Archaeological Survey of India, the National Museum and the National Gallery of Modern Art, whose collections it has helped bring to wider audiences over the years.
Mr Amit Sood, Vice President and Founder, Google Arts & Culture, said: “For the past 15 years, Google Arts & Culture has been deeply inspired by India’s millennia of storytelling, artistic mastery and vast heritage. Our partnership with the Ministry of Culture represents a shared commitment to preserve India’s timeless treasures with the help of cutting-edge technologies. Whether supporting the vision for the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum or preserving historic manuscripts, we are honoured to deploy our technologies to bridge ancient heritage with modern accessibility, making these collections freely discoverable to educate, inspire, and delight curious minds everywhere.”
The MoU reaffirms the Ministry’s commitment to preserving India’s civilisational heritage, championing its creative economy through enduring partnerships, and sharing its culture with the widest possible networks at home and across the world.

title: IPRD-2026 CONCLUDES WITH FOCUS ON COOPERATIVE OCEAN GOVERNANCE AND RESPONSIBLE MARITIME TECHNOLOGIES
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                05 NOV 2026 7:20PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The three-day Indo-Pacific Regional Dialogue 2026 (IPRD-2026), the Indian Navy’s annual apex-level international strategic dialogue, concluded on
05 Nov 2026
in New Delhi. Organised in association with the National Maritime Foundation (NMF), the conference examined
‘Science, Technology and Academic Cooperation in the Indo-Pacific’
through five professional thematic sessions and senior-level interactions intended to identify practical pathways for regional maritime cooperation.
The concluding day opened with a
Special Address by Gen NS Raja Subramani, Chief of Defence Staff
, after which the CDS had an engaging interaction with the audience. This was followed by a session on
‘Collaborative Approaches to Ocean Governance and Maritime Resilience’
, moderated by VAdm Sanjay Jasjit Singh (Retd), Director-General, United Service Institution of India.  In this session, Professor Deo Florence Onda of the University of the Philippines addressed a cooperative plan to share Filipino experience and expertise in ocean governance. Dr Marie Bourrel-McKinnon, former Chief of Staff in the International Seabed Authority, examined equitable deep-sea research partnerships and resource governance. Mr Ramraj Narasimhan, from the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI), provided an overview of the implementation of the Infrastructure for Resilient Island States (IRIS) programme, while Ms Sofia Furstenberg-Stott of Future Maritime, Sweden, considered how the interface between marine science and shipping operations could be strengthened. The session brought together four dimensions of a common challenge: the need to link scientific capability with governance, make research partnerships more equitable, strengthen the resilience of vulnerable island states, and ensure that scientific knowledge informs the decisions of maritime industry and public institutions.
The final session of IPRD-2026 was centred on the theme, ‘
Transformative Maritime Technologies and Dual-Use Implications’
.  This session was moderated by Rear Admiral Guninder Singh Jawanda (Retd), Indian Navy. In this session, speakers addressed distinct facets of the sessional theme. Ms Dongyoun Cho of the International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS), Germany, examined a practical framework for Indo-Pacific cooperation on artificial intelligence and quantum technologies in the maritime domain. Dr Eva Pejsova from the Brussels School of Governance addressed EU–Indo-Pacific mechanisms for the responsible governance of dual-use maritime technologies. Captain Mark Blaine (Retd), South African Navy, from Stellenbosch University discussed a cooperation roadmap to help small and medium navies adapt to these technologies, while Commodore Arun Golaya (Retd) considered operational Navy-to-Navy cooperation for their responsible adoption.  The discussions reflected the dual character of emerging maritime technologies and examined the potential for collaborative research, practical capacity-building and institutional arrangements that allow partners with differing resources and requirements to participate meaningfully in technological change.
The Valedictory Address by
Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh, Defence Secretary, Government of India,
brought the mega three-day conference to a fitting and memorable closure. Over its three days, the IPRD-2026 witnessed participation by a wide spectrum of military practitioners, policy makers, representatives from the maritime industry, diplomats from India and friendly foreign countries, academia, media, eminent citizens, and New Delhi’s vibrant student community. Over forty experts and distinguished speakers from twenty countries shared their perspectives on the IPRD’s unifying theme of
‘Science, Technology and Academic Cooperation in the Indo-Pacific’
, providing greater specificity to actionable outcomes under the Science, Technology and Academic Cooperation pillar of the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative.  The conference also bolstered the Indian Navy’s committed stance on enhancing regional maritime security and promoting collaborative approaches to strengthen maritime resilience, thus providing a clearer expression to India’s maritime vision of
MAHASAGAR
(Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions)
.

The initiative reinforces the Government of India's commitment to efficient public asset management, transparent and value-maximising monetisation, and productive utilisation of surplus assets to support investment and economic development.

The National Land Monetization Corporation (NLMC) is a wholly owned Government of India company under the administrative control of the Department of Public Enterprises, Ministry of Finance. It was informed that the Phase-I buildings, including the OPD Registration Block, OPD Block, residential buildings and designated hostels, have been completed, with inventory verification and formal handover processes underway. The remaining academic, administrative, hospital, residential and hostel infrastructure is being taken up in a phased manner.
Emphasising the need for early operationalisation of the Institute, Shri Nadda directed HITES and the Executive Director, AIIMS Awantipora, to work in close coordination and expedite the procurement of medical equipment, OPD instruments, laboratory equipment and medical and administrative furniture. He stressed that all essential procurements required for commencement of OPD services must be completed on priority.

content:
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today inaugurated the Martyrs’ Memorial of the First War of Independence of 1857 in Ambala, Haryana. On this occasion, Haryana Chief Minister Shri Nayab Singh Saini and Union Minister Shri Manohar Lal, along with many other dignitaries, were present.
On this occasion, in his address, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Minister Shri Amit Shah said that on this very land, on 10th May 1857, the revolutionary heroes had sounded the bugle of armed revolution against British rule, and from here that revolution had spread like fire, leaving the entire world astonished. British-inspired historians of leftist ideology termed the freedom struggle of 1857 a mere revolt. It may have been a revolt for the British, but Veer Savarkar had said that the revolution of 1857 was not a revolt for the children of Mother India, but a freedom struggle. It was the revolution of 1857 that ignited the flame of freedom in the heart of every citizen of this vast country stretching from the Himalayas to Kanyakumari and from Gangasagar to Somnath.
Shri Amit Shah said that in this great struggle of 90 years from 1857 to 1947, countless martyrs sacrificed everything they had, and only then did we get the good fortune to see present-day India and Mother India. On the foundation of those martyrs’ sacrifices, today under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, we can envision a developed India. Building on the sacrifices of those martyrs and strengthening democratic institutions for 80 years, we stand with dignity before the entire world. The warriors of the 1857 revolution — Nana Saheb Peshwa, Rani Lakshmibai, Tatya Tope, Begum Hazrat Mahal,  and many other fighters — displayed their valour and made the supreme sacrifice.
Union Home Minister said that no country truly understands the value of its freedom until it glorifies the martyrs who shed their blood for it. A country that does not rewrite the blood-stained pages of history in golden letters can never progress. This Martyrs’ Memorial built today in Ambala will become a source of boundless patriotic inspiration for our coming generations of youth and adolescents.
Shri Amit Shah stated that the Saraswati once flowed across this very sacred land, and it was from here—in the region extending as far as the Ganga-Yamuna Doab—that the Vedas and Upanishads were composed. On this very land, Lord Shri Krishna recited the Gita. On this brave land, Maharaja Agrasen gave the Indian model of administration. On this brave land, Raja Nahar Singh and Rao Tula Ram fought the freedom struggle, and continuing that tradition, today a small state like Haryana contributes the highest number of soldiers to the Army. In India’s sports medal tallies, Haryana consistently ranks number one. When the country needed to become self-reliant in food grains, the farmers of Haryana filled the nation’s granaries. Haryana has also made a very significant contribution to the White Revolution.
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Minister said that today, on the land of Haryana, a magnificent memorial of the 1857 revolution has been built on 22 acres at a cost of ₹594 crore, featuring 22 galleries. Shri Shah stated that this memorial represents a remarkable effort to weave together historical documents and the diverse art forms of Haryana, utilizing modern technology such as virtual reality, holography, and interactive projection. With Phulkari and Sarkanda craftsmanship, an open-air theatre seating 2,500 people, and a light-and-sound show, the memorial has been designed to transport visitors back to 1857. This memorial has become a vibrant space that awakens pride in the glory, sacrifice and honour of the 1857 revolution and a sense of duty towards the nation. An appeal is made to the youth of the entire country: to understand the people because of whom we stand where we are today, please visit this memorial in Ambala and also pay homage to the martyrs.
Shri Amit Shah said that today a National Highway built at a cost of ₹1,260 crore was also inaugurated, and through this highway Haryana will become a state with excellent connectivity. Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, our government has brought about fundamental transformation in Haryana. With the delivery of gas cylinders to every household, Haryana became the country’s first smoke-free state. Haryana is the only state in India that procures 24 crops at MSP. It became the first state to implement the new criminal codes and increase the conviction rate by 40%. Haryana became the first state to operate a hydrogen train. The country’s first elevated railway track was also started in Haryana. Under the Haryana Antyodaya Parivar Parivahan Yojana (HAPPY), an initiative was also implemented in Haryana to provide 1,000 kilometers of free travel to poor families. The country’s largest Transgender Welfare Board was set up in Haryana. The practice of having fully literate panchayats was also pioneered in Haryana. An online transfer policy was formulated in Haryana, and our government completely eliminated the transfer industry from the state. Haryana is the only state in the entire country where there is no longer any ‘Lal Dora’ in the villages. Haryana has become an anaemia-free state, the country’s first Ayush school was established here, it became the first state to issue ‘Parivar Pehchan Patra’, and it is also the first state to stand with farmers of horticultural crops through the Bhavantar scheme. Haryana also pays the highest wages under MGNREGA. Over the past 60 years, Haryana has made remarkable progress. The state has also geared up for a drug-free Haryana, and Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has given priority to Haryana.
