Timeline for Commissioning
Beneficiaries must commission the plant within
three years
of the Letter of Award (LoA). In any case, commissioning must be completed within
five years
of the LoA. If commissioning is delayed beyond three years, the remaining undisbursed CAPEX support will be subject to a tapering mechanism until the fifth year.
Governance Framework
A
three-tier governance structure
will oversee the scheme. It will ensure effective execution, monitoring and guidance.
Tier
Body
Key Role
Apex
Governing Council (GC), chaired by the Secretary, Ministry of Mines
Provides strategic guidance and reviews progress. Makes final selection of beneficiaries and sanctions CAPEX support. It is also empowered to approve amendments to scheme guidelines, subject to the approval of the Union Minister of Mines.
Evaluation
Techno-Financial Committee (TFC)
Evaluates applications on technical and financial grounds. Recommends beneficiaries to the GC. Includes technical and financial experts from R&D bodies, technical institutions and PSUs.
Implementation
Project Management Agency (PMA)
Provides secretarial, managerial and implementation support. Carries out other tasks assigned by the Ministry of Mines.
Why Domestic Processing Matters
Domestic processing capacity is central to India’s critical mineral security and self-reliance. The key reasons for building this capacity are outlined below:
Strategic Importance:
Resilient domestic value chains are vital for energy transition technologies, defence, aerospace and speciality steel. Domestic processing can reduce external supply risks and support self-reliance. It also addresses India’s limited access to cost-effective technologies, intermediate compounds and technical expertise.
Strong Domestic Demand:
Demand projections show a clear need to build local processing capacity. Developing domestic capacity is essential for maximising value addition and achieving import substitution.
Barriers to Investment:
Domestic processing is currently not viable under prevailing market conditions. Projects need advanced equipment, multi-stage conversion systems and strict environmental safeguards, which raise capital costs. Access to raw materials and suitable technologies is also limited. Without targeted support, industries find it hard to set up such plants.
Expected Outcomes
The scheme is expected to deliver economic and strategic benefits:
Investment and Capacity:
The scheme is expected to attract about
₹10,000 crore
in processing investment. It will support the creation of
60 kt of Lithium
and
100 kt of Nickel
processing capacity to meet projected demand by 2030.
Domestic Value Addition:
Ores, concentrates and intermediates will be processed into high-purity products within India. This will help capture a larger share of the value chain domestically.
Supply Security:
The scheme is expected to reduce India's exposure to geographically concentrated processing and potential export restrictions.
Lower Import Bill:
Domestic production of high-purity intermediates is expected to substitute imports, reducing the import bill and foreign exchange outgo.
Support for Downstream Manufacturing:
Refined outputs will support battery material, battery cell and speciality steel manufacturing, strengthening existing downstream schemes.
Employment Generation:
The scheme is expected to generate direct and indirect employment in critical mineral processing. Increased manufacturing of end-use products could create further employment opportunities.
Strengthening India’s Critical Mineral Ecosystem
The scheme complements several initiatives already underway across the critical mineral value chain. Together, they now cover exploration, mining, recycling and processing.
National Critical Mineral Mission (NCMM):
Launched in January 2025, NCMM secures a long-term supply of critical minerals and strengthens the entire value chain. Under the Mission, a ₹1,500 crore
recycling scheme approved by the Union Cabinet on 3rd September 2025
promotes the recovery of critical minerals from secondary sources. These include e-waste, spent lithium-ion batteries and other scrap.
Exploration and Mining:
Auctions of mineral blocks have gained steady momentum.
So far, 64
critical and strategic mineral blocks and 11 Exploration Licence blocks were auctioned
by the Central Government
.
Way Forward
The
CAPEX Support Scheme to Promote Critical Mineral Processing
fills a crucial gap in India’s critical mineral value chain. By supporting Lithium and Nickel processing, it will reduce import dependence and strengthen supply chain resilience. Alongside the National Critical Mineral Mission, it marks an important step towards the vision of
Atmanirbhar Bharat
.

title: NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported sexual abuse of two teachers at a private school by the owner's brother in Aligarh district, Uttar Pradesh
subtitle: Issues notices to the Aligarh District Magistrate and Senior Superintendent of Police, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                05 NOV 2026 4:54PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken
suo motu
cognizance of a media report that two teachers were subjected to sexual abuse at a private school in Aligarh district, Uttar Pradesh. Reportedly, one of the teachers alleged that she was sexually harassed by the brother of the owner of the school for a long time. When she objected to it, he threatened to get her removed from the service. The other teacher had also faced similar harassment and was removed from service when she objected to it.
The Commission has observed that the contents of the news report, if true, raise serious issues of human rights violations. Therefore, it has issued notices to the Aligarh District Magistrate and Senior Superintendent of Police, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks.
According to the media report, carried on 3
rd
November 2026, the school management has not taken any action on the victims' complaints. Therefore, they have approached the SSP requesting legal action.

title: NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported death of a 12-year-old student after coming into contact with an 11 KV power line passing close to the roof of the school building in Ballia district, Uttar Pradesh
subtitle:
Reportedly, teachers asked him to climb and pluck a ‘bottle gourd’ from the kitchen roof for the mid-day meal

date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:

content:
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken
suo motu
cognizance of a media report that on 2nd November 2026, a 12-year-old fourth-standard student of a government primary school died after coming into contact with an 11 KV power line passing close to the roof of the school building in Ballia district, Uttar Pradesh. Reportedly, the teachers asked him to climb and pluck a ‘bottle gourd’ from the kitchen roof for the mid-day meal.
The Commission has observed that the contents of the news report, if true, raise serious issues of violation of human rights. Therefore, it has issued notices to the Chairman-cum-Managing Director, Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Ltd. (UPPCL), Ballia District Magistrate and the Superintendent of Police, Ballia, calling for detailed reports on the matter within two weeks.
According to a media report, carried on 3
rd
November 2026, two teachers of the school have been placed under suspension and a recommendation has been made for termination of the services of the Shiksha Mitra

title: NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported deaths of 24 women in seven months this year during pregnancy treatment or childbirth at different government and private hospitals in Ghaziabad district, Uttar Pradesh
subtitle:
Reportedly, more than 3,000 pregnant women identified having high-risk pregnancies in the district

The Commission issues notices to the Principal Secretary, Department of Medical Health & Family Welfare, Uttar Pradesh and DM, Ghaziabad, calling for detailed reports on the matter within two weeks
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                05 NOV 2026 4:50PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken
suo motu
cognizance of a media report that from April to October 2026, 24 women died during pregnancy treatment or childbirth at different government and private hospitals in Ghaziabad district, Uttar Pradesh. This information was disclosed in a report of the Health Department. The Rajapur area recorded the highest number of deaths at 8, followed by Loni and Bhojpur with 5 deaths each. Reportedly, more than 3,000 pregnant women in the district have been identified as having high-risk pregnancies.
The Commission has observed that the contents of the news report, if true, raise serious issues of violation of human rights. Therefore, it has issued notices to the Principal Secretary, Department of Medical Health & Family Welfare, Uttar Pradesh and District Magistrate, Ghaziabad, calling for detailed reports on the matter within two weeks.
According to the media report, carried on 3
rd
November 2026, 10 out of 24 women died due to excessive bleeding, 3 due to severe infection and 3 others due to hypertension. The remaining eight deaths were reportedly attributed to other medical conditions, including anaemia, heart attack, tuberculosis and brain tumour.

title: NHRC, India’s intervention leads to establishment of a Gender-Neutral Cell at Central Prison, Hyderabad for persons with diverse gender identities and expressions
subtitle: The Prison authorities also permit affirmative clothing for persons accommodated in the Gender-Neutral Cell
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                05 NOV 2026 11:41AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has been informed by the Hyderabad Central Prison authorities that they have established a separate Gender-Neutral Cell for persons with diverse gender identities and expressions to ensure their dignity and appropriate living arrangements.
The move followed a visit to the Prison on 8th October 2026 by the Commission’s Special Monitor, entrusted with matters relating to transgender persons and the rights of the LGBTQ+ community. During his visit, the implementation of the NHRC and MHA advisories was emphasised for ensuring the welfare of transgender persons.
In its compliance report, the Superintendent of Central Prison, Hyderabad informed the Commission that the recommendations to set up a Gender-Neutral Cell have been implemented. Besides this, the Prison authorities have also permitted affirmative clothing for persons accommodated in the facility.
The initiative reflects the Commission's efforts to promote the protection of the human rights and dignity of persons with diverse gender identities and expressions in correctional institutions.
